papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet a large proportion of patients do not respond. The lung microbiome is a key modulator of antitumor immunity, however, the functional contribution of active microbial communities and their interaction with host transcriptional programs in shaping ICI outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we prospectively analyzed bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples from 71 NSCLC patients prior to ICI initiation. We profiled the microbiome and host transcriptome in the BAL to look for microbial and host signatures in the lower airways associated with treatment response. We found that enrichment of the lower airway microbiome with oral commensals was associated with disease progression and worse prognosis of patients treated with ICI. Metatranscriptomics-derived microbial clustering revealed distinct functional profiles. The microbial cluster enriched with oral commensals, which was only present among patients with poor response to ICI, had differential regulation of pathways involved in the metabolism of short-chain fatty acids, methane, and pyruvate. This cluster also correlated with host immune pathways including upregulation of interferon signaling, neutrophil degranulation, and mitophagy, all of which could contribute to the poor response to immunotherapy. In a preclinical murine model of lung cancer with dysbiosis, inoculating lung tumor-bearing mice with oral commensals increased intratumoral neutrophils and Th17 responses and impaired ICI efficacy. Our findings support the concept that microbial communities in the lower airways influence tumor-immune interactions via defined metabolic-immune axes.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: COPE evaluated serial circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling with molecular tumor board (MTB) review during first-line therapy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: COPE was a multicenter, randomized (2:1), noncomparative phase II trial. Arm A underwent serial plasma profiling with every report reviewed at a weekly virtual MTB; Arm B received standard management. The primary endpoint was 18-month overall survival (OS) in Arm A versus a prespecified 40% historical benchmark; no between-arm comparison was planned. RESULTS: Among 176 patients, 117 were assigned to Arm A and 59 to Arm B. Eighteen-month OS was 53.8% (95% CI, 44.3-62.5) and 65.7% (95% CI, 52.0-76.3), respectively. Baseline plasma profiling provided contributory information in 32 of 35 patients with noncontributory or unavailable tissue, increasing genotyping success from 69% to 97%. Paired baseline and early on-treatment samples were available in 90 patients (median, 21 days; range, 19-64). ctDNA clearance was associated with higher objective response rate (83% vs. 52%), longer progression-free survival (22.9 vs. 5.4 months; P<0.001), and longer OS (not reached vs. 17.1 months; P=0.004) than persistent detection. CONCLUSIONS: Serial ctDNA profiling with weekly MTB review was operationally feasible and complemented tissue genotyping. Clinical benefit was not demonstrated; early ctDNA kinetics require validation in interventional trials.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Radiation therapy (RT) is indicated for 77% of patients with lung cancer. Over 20% of patients are affected by radiation-induced lung injury. Computed tomography ventilation imaging (CTVI) estimates high and low functioning lung regions. During RT planning, CTVI can guide preferential avoidance of higher ventilated regions by redirecting dose to less well ventilated regions, sparing healthy lung tissue. The double-masked randomized Trans-Tasman Radiation Oncology Group (TROG) 21.08 VITaL trial will investigate if sparing healthy lung can improve the quality of life (QoL) for patients with stage 3 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT. METHODS: 165 patients will be recruited to test the hypothesis that patients receiving healthy lung-sparing RT have better QoL than patients receiving standard RT. CTVI will be generated from exhale and inhale breath-hold CT scan pairs. A healthy lung-sparing plan and a standard treatment plan will be created for each patient and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio for the patient's treatment. QoL will be assessed with the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung questionnaire before and after treatment. Secondary hypotheses include that patients in the healthy lung-sparing arm will have fewer treatment side effects, better lung function, be more likely to receive and complete adjuvant immunotherapy, and healthy lung-sparing treatment will be cost-effective. Patient follow-up will continue for three years. DISCUSSION: This prospective randomized trial will determine whether the incorporation of healthy lung-sparing RT based on CTVI improves QoL, reduces pulmonary toxicity, and increases eligibility to receive curative immunotherapy for patients with stage 3 NSCLC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06127654).

papers.abstract_en: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CREBBP loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in Rb1/Trp53-driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently, Crebbp deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically, Crebbp loss suppresses Sting and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both Crebbp-mutant and Crebbp-wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in Crebbp-mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish CREBBP loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: Lung reirradiation is seeing increased use, yet the evidence base guiding its practice remains limited despite significant technological advances. This paper provides a consensus approach addressing the technical factors underpinning clinical decision-making. It aims to answer the central question: how can clinical teams implement a safe, reproducible, and technically robust workflow for high-dose lung reirradiation? The recommendations are developed by an expert panel of radiation oncologists, medical physicists, and radiation therapists (RTT) from 14 European, American, and Canadian centres, synthesizing a broad range of clinical perspectives. The scope of this work/manuscript is to provide a structured, practical workflow applicable across diverse clinical settings. Using a clinical case, the manuscript demonstrates key conceptual principles, such as the rationale for advanced dose accumulation and the impact of anatomical changes during treatment, with clear, stepwise guidance to support consistent implementation and informed clinical judgement. Key recommended steps include retrieval of prior treatment data; consideration of prior positioning and motion management; and equieffective dose accumulation using deformable image registration or organ-at-risk (OAR)-focused rigid registration. Treatment planning should explicitly incorporate prior dose while balancing target coverage against OAR limits. Daily online volumetric image guidance is central to evaluating both bony and soft-tissue anatomy, enabling setup adjustments to protect critical structures approaching tolerance. Clear documentation and multidisciplinary communication are integral throughout. This consensus approach is intended to support both centres that aim to establish reirradiation practice and experienced teams seeking to harmonize best practices.

papers.abstract_en: This letter to the Editor addresses a fundamental inconsistency in the reporting of study design and validation status in the article by Zhou et al. published in Cancer Imaging. The authors state in the Methods section that the study retrospectively analyzed 125 patients, yet the Introduction and Discussion claim that the study prospectively validated the prognostic value of early tumour shrinkage (ETS) and depth of response (DoR). Prospective validation requires a priori model specification and evaluation on subsequently collected data, whereas retrospective analyses are inherently susceptible to selection bias and cannot establish prospective validity. The authors also conclude that they developed and validated a comprehensive predictive model, but no external validation, temporal validation, or clearly described internal validation procedure is reported. The ETS and DoR thresholds were derived from ROC analysis within the same cohort and then applied to the same patients for survival analysis, risking overfitting and optimistic bias. Additionally, the Results report "responders (n = 109) and non-responders (n = 12)," while the corresponding results in the original article by Zhou et al. [1] list the ratio as 12/109, reversing the group labels. We respectfully suggest that the authors clarify the actual study design, remove any claim of prospective validation if the study is retrospective, provide evidence of validation or remove the claim of a validated model, and correct the numerical inconsistency. Such corrections would uphold the scientific integrity of the literature.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. papers.abstract_en: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have marked a turning point in the treatment of oncogene-addicted non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), offering unprecedented efficacy. Yet, most tumors eventually develop resistance and progress, often prompting discontinuation of the targeted agent and a switch to non-targeted therapies such as chemotherapy. We explored current evidence on maintaining inhibition of the oncogenic driver beyond progression in a narrative literature review through August 24, 2026, including clinical trials, retrospective analyses, case reports, case series, and preclinical models. Among all drivers, only EGFR-mutated NSCLC provided phase II/III evidence supporting maintenance of driver inhibition beyond progression. Combinations of EGFR-directed therapies with chemotherapy or MET inhibitors were associated with improved response rates and progression-free survival (PFS) compared with chemotherapy or MET inhibitor monotherapy, although these trials had several limitations. ALK and KRAS G12C evidence was limited to early-phase trials with small cohorts and modest clinical signals, while the remaining drivers (RET, METex14, NTRK, HER2, ROS1, BRAF, and EGFR exon 20) evidence was largely preclinical or anecdotal, making continuation experimental. Co-occurring resistance mechanisms, heterogeneous tumor evolution, and potential additive toxicity complicate interpretation of the backbone's contribution to clinical benefit. Continuation should therefore not be applied routinely but tailored to the pattern and site of progression, re-biopsy findings, CNS disease control, expected toxicity, and patient preferences. Given the rarity of many oncogenic drivers and the challenges of conducting adequately powered randomized trials, definitive data may remain available for several resistance scenarios.

papers.abstract_en: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRASG12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRASG12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS-driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) remains an aggressive malignancy with poor survival despite platinum-etoposide chemotherapy. Although serplulimab plus chemotherapy has demonstrated a survival benefit in randomized trials, comparative real-world evidence remains limited. We therefore evaluated survival outcomes with first-line serplulimab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in patients with ES-SCLC. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study at Tianjin Chest Hospital. Patients with ES-SCLC who initiated first-line platinum-etoposide-based chemotherapy between January 2020 and December 2024 were screened, with follow-up censored on May 1, 2025. Patients were classified according to whether serplulimab was incorporated into first-line treatment. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), and the secondary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS). Treatment effects were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models. Because of the limited sample size and event count, the primary adjusted Cox model was restricted to prespecified clinical covariates. Sensitivity analyses included treatment-year adjustment, restriction to patients treated during 2022-2024, reduced propensity score overlap weighting and stabilized trimmed inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). RESULTS: The final cohort included 112 patients, of whom 30 received serplulimab plus chemotherapy and 82 received chemotherapy alone. Median OS was 18.69 months with serplulimab plus chemotherapy and 11.86 months with chemotherapy alone (HR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.27-0.90; P = 0.021; log-rank P = 0.017). The association remained significant after parsimonious clinical adjustment (adjusted HR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.27-0.93; P = 0.028). Sensitivity analyses yielded directionally similar OS estimates across treatment-year adjustment, 2022-2024 restriction, overlap weighting, and stabilized trimmed IPTW. Median rwPFS was also numerically longer with serplulimab plus chemotherapy, although the difference was not statistically significant (10.64 vs 8.18 months; HR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.48-1.20; P = 0.244). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center real-world cohort, first-line serplulimab plus chemotherapy was associated with longer OS than chemotherapy alone in patients with ES-SCLC, whereas the rwPFS difference was not statistically significant. The findings were directionally supported by multiple sensitivity analyses but should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, potential calendar-time confounding, and incomplete standardized safety assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed for confirmation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The optimal integration of surgery and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) following modern neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains controversial. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have substantially improved outcomes in both resectable and unresectable disease, prospective randomized data directly comparing surgery and definitive CRT after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy are lacking. METHODS: InDuRanS is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial conducted in Germany. Patients with (borderline) resectable stage IIB-IIIA/B (N2) NSCLC receive three cycles of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy with durvalumab plus platinum-paclitaxel. Patients with persistent resectability are randomized 1:1 to surgery or definitive CRT. Both treatment arms receive consolidation durvalumab for up to 12 months. The primary endpoint is 2-year event-free survival in 158 randomized patients. Key secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety and tolerability, health-related quality of life, and an extensive exploratory translational research program. DISCUSSION: InDuRanS is the first randomized trial to directly compare surgery versus definitive CRT within a contemporary multimodal treatment sequence incorporating both neoadjuvant and consolidation immunotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B NSCLC. Its results are expected to help define optimal local treatment strategies in an evolving therapeutic landscape. InDuRanS is currently active and open to enrollment as of April 2025, with primary completion anticipated in 2028 (NCT06810609).

papers.abstract_en: It remains largely unclear whether oncogenic super-enhancers (SEs) can drive expression of circular RNAs (circRNAs). In this study, we for the first time profiled the comprehensive circRNA landscapes of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) after suppressing genome-wide SE activities. We identified a novel SE-driven circPRRC2B, as the product of back-splicing of exons 2, 3, 4 and 5 of PRRC2B pre-mRNA, which was controlled by RNA binding protein HuR. Indeed, SE drives high levels of PRRC2B transcription, promotes production of PRRC2B pre-mRNAs, boosts back-splicing of PRRC2B pre-mRNAs, and elevates circPRRC2B expression. ETS1 acts as a key transcriptional factor in SE-driven PRRC2B transcription and circPRRC2B biogenesis. Interestingly, circPRRC2B, but not PRRC2B, could promote proliferation, invasion and metastasis of ESCC in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, circPRRC2B binds to TALDO1 and enhances BAP1-mediated TALDO1 de-ubiquitination in ESCC cells. Therefore, circPRRC2B stabilizes and sustains high expression of TALDO1, activates the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), elevates the glutathione levels via supplying more NADPH via the PPP, inhibits production of reactive oxygen species in mitochondrion, maintains cellular redox equilibrium, and, thus, leads to cancer progression. Importantly, we developed antisense oligonucleotides targeting circPRRC2B which exhibited remarkable inhibition of ESCC growth. Our findings highlighted circPRRC2B as a key target preserving the PPP metabolic flux and redox homeostasis of malignant cells, thereby offering insight into developing novel therapeutics for cancers.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: If metastasis can be predicted, appropriate management of lung cancer will be possible to improve prognosis. Therefore, the main objective of this study is to develop a prediction model with appropriate performance for predicting metastasis based on patient data. METHODS: The study analyzed patient records from Kaggle, performing exploratory data analysis and preprocessing techniques such as missing values handling, encoding categorical variables, and outliers' removal. Next, Data normalization and feature engineering were applied. Imbalanced data was addressed using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Supervised classification models, including boosting algorithms were developed and tuned via Grid Search algorithms. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC, with stratified k-fold cross-validation ensuring robustness. All processes were conducted using Python language on Google Collab. RESULTS: After data preprocessing, normalization, and selecting more related features, the dataset was stratified into training and testing subsets using an 80:20 split to ensure representative sampling classification models trained on training data. Class imbalance in the target variable was addressed using the SMOTE on the training set to balance classes without biasing the test set. Various machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, KNN, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and boosting algorithms (AdaBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting), were developed and evaluated using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC. SMOTE significantly improved model performance, with XGBoost emerging as the top performer, achieving the highest AUC (82%) and F1-score (74.83%). ROC curve analysis confirmed XGBoost's superior predictive power for metastasis. CONCLUSIONS: The development of a high-performing prediction model for lung cancer metastasis to other organs has significant implications for clinical practice. Early and accurate prediction of metastasis can enable timely interventions, potentially improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cachexia in oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is driven by systemic inflammation and malnutrition and is associated with poor survival. We evaluated whether circulating miRNAs can identify ESCC cachexia and reflect its inflammatory-nutritional phenotype. METHODS: We enrolled 126 participants: 42 healthy controls and 84 treatment-naïve patients with ESCC, equally classified as noncachectic or cachectic using international consensus criteria. Small-RNA sequencing in a discovery subset (n = 4/group) was followed by cohort-wide qRT-PCR. Exploratory within-cohort discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis; survival associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and univariate Cox analyses. RESULTS: Cachectic ESCC was characterized by lower albumin, total protein and prealbumin and higher IL-6, TNF-α, CRP and IL-1β than noncachectic ESCC (all p < 0.05). Circulating hsa-miR-5187-5p and hsa-miR-4433b-3p increased stepwise from controls to noncachectic and cachectic ESCC. For noncachectic versus cachectic ESCC, AUCs were 0.8594 and 0.8175, respectively (both p < 0.0001); for controls versus cachectic ESCC, AUCs were 0.9439 and 0.8889. Cachexia was associated with shorter overall survival (HR 1.708, 95% CI 1.011-2.887; p = 0.026), as were high miR-5187-5p (HR 3.635) and miR-4433b-3p (HR 3.190) expression. Correlations with inflammatory markers and albumin were weak to moderate. CONCLUSIONS: hsa-miR-5187-5p and hsa-miR-4433b-3p are candidate circulating indicators of ESCC-associated cachexia and its inflammatory-metabolic milieu. Their discriminatory and prognostic performance remains exploratory because analyses were conducted within the same cohort and were not comprehensively adjusted for tumour stage or other clinicopathological factors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The tumour immune microenvironment influences neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy success in esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Complete responders show higher treatment-naïve intratumoral CD8+ T cell levels before treatment than non-complete responders. Understanding mechanisms driving CD8+ T cells exclusion from the TIME is essential to improving outcomes. METHODS: We performed spatial transcriptomics on treatment-naive CD8-low and high EACs (N = 12). Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected based on tumour annotation by a pathologist. Cancer (CK+) cells and immune (CD45+) cells were analysed within the same ROI. Findings were validated using bulk transcriptome data (TCGA) and metabolic profiling (SCENITH) of fresh tumour specimen (n = 5). RESULTS: Whole transcriptomic profiling showed cancer cell clustering based on T cell infiltration. Cancer cell transcriptomes of CD8-low tumours exhibited reduced antigen presentation and upregulated lipid and mitochondrial metabolism, while CD8-high tumours showed increased cytokine signalling and apoptotic pathways. In CD45+ compartments, CD8-low tumours were enriched for the PGC-1α pathway, linked to mitochondrial biogenesis and immunosuppressive myeloid populations. These findings were supported by TCGA data. SCENITH confirmed mitochondrial dependence of macrophages in CD8-low tumours. CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that mitochondrial metabolism and impaired antigen presentation contribute to T cell exclusion in EAC. These findings raise the hypothesis that targeting mitochondrial metabolism in these cancers can modulate the anti-tumour immune response and thereby improve the response to chemoradiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundLoss of appetite (LOA) is a highly prevalent and distressing symptom in advanced lung cancer, leading to malnutrition, poorer treatment tolerance, and reduced quality of life. Although acupuncture may help manage cancer-related symptoms, its effect on LOA in patients receiving immunotherapy is unclear. This study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for alleviating LOA in this population.MethodsThis multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will enroll 80 eligible patients with advanced lung cancer undergoing immunotherapy who experience LOA, defined as a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) score ≥30 mm. Participants will be randomly assigned to either true acupuncture or sham acupuncture in a 1:1 ratio, administered over 24 sessions within a 12-week period. The primary outcome is the LOA response rate at week 12. Secondary outcomes include changes in LOA severity, nutritional and hematologic markers, patient-reported measures (appetite/cachexia, disease symptoms, psychological distress, and sleep), and tumor response. Safety and blinding success will also be assessed. Data will be analyzed using SPSS 20.0 and R software.DiscussionTo our knowledge, this is the first rigorously designed trial evaluating acupuncture for LOA in advanced lung cancer patients undergoing immunotherapy. The findings may inform integrative supportive care strategies for this patient population.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Organ-specific dose estimates are needed to characterize radiation exposure from repeated low-dose computed tomography (CT) lung cancer screening in the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). The objective was to estimate study-level doses and participant-level cumulative doses in the NLST CT screening cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective dosimetry study included 25,051 NLST CT screening participants from the Lung Screening Study and American College of Radiology Imaging Network components after excluding participants with any examination lacking a valid manufacturer-appropriate tube current-time input. Image-series metadata were linked with age, sex, height, and weight, and then valid records were grouped into 69,601 study-level screening examinations. Organ absorbed doses and effective dose were calculated using the National Cancer Institute dosimetry system for Computed Tomography with sex- and body-size-specific adult phantoms. Scan-range-related dose uncertainty was assessed with 50 stochastic simulations. RESULTS: Participants underwent a mean of 2.78 study-level screening examinations; the median study-level volume CT dose index was 3.30 mGy. Median (interquartile range) study-level lung, breast, heart wall, active marrow, and effective doses were 3.93 (3.13-4.96), 3.94 (3.14-5.04), 3.94 (3.14-5.01), and 1.26 (0.99-1.60) mGy, and 2.07 (1.65-2.59) mSv, respectively. Corresponding cumulative participant-level doses were 11.30 (8.89-14.50), 11.39 (9.01-14.75), 11.41 (8.93-14.66), and 3.63 (2.79-4.66) mGy, and 5.94 (4.69-7.64) mSv. Scan-range-related dose uncertainty was greatest for thyroid dose (mean coefficient of variation, 21.1%) and low for in-field organs. CONCLUSION: Using NLST low-dose CT screening data, we estimated participant-level cumulative organ and effective doses and characterized variation across organs and body-size groups.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies. DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies. RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24). CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The tumor microenvironment exerts intense survival pressure on CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), yet the cellular basis for an earlier, less-exhausted state associated with response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We previously identified BCL2A1 as a CD8+ TIL-derived marker predictive of a response to PD-1 blockade. Here we combine deep single-cell discovery with experimental validation in primary human T cells to characterise the BCL2A1-associated CD8+ TIL state and its candidate upstream signal. METHODS: We integrated four transcriptomic cohorts-pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq with CD8+ TIL deconvolution (n=60), on-treatment scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=11), longitudinal scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=18), and an independent post-treatment cohort (n=59)-with in silico perturbation, pathway, and metabolic-flux analyses, and experimentally tested a key prediction of this state by flow cytometry in primary human CD8+ T cells. RESULTS: BCL2A1 high CD8+ TILs showed elevated BCL2A1 expression without coordinated upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family genes, maintained minimal exhaustion, and occupied an early, BCL6-, TCF7-, and NFKB1-regulated pseudotime state. Across longitudinal and post-treatment cohorts, they formed diverse, low-expansion repertoires rather than dominant expanded clones, with reduced biosynthetic flux (branched-chain amino acid and purine metabolism) consistent with a non-proliferative state. NF-κB signaling was elevated, and TNF-α was nominated as the leading candidate upstream ligand of BCL2A1. We then experimentally tested this prediction: in primary human CD8+ T cells, TNF-α induced BCL2A1 protein ≈13-fold (44.5% vs. 3.4% BCL2A1+; MFI 2.93-fold; P < 0.0001), whereas CD3/CD28 activation alone did not, establishing a TNF-α-specific, protein-level response. CONCLUSIONS: Combining integrative single-cell analysis with experimental validation in primary human T cells, we define BCL2A1 as a marker of an early, less-exhausted CD8+ TIL state associated with improved ICB outcomes in NSCLC; a survival-related role is supported by these associations but was not functionally tested.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are being investigated in advanced small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the evidence is dominated by early-phase studies conducted in non-exchangeable treatment settings. We evaluated the activity and toxicity of ADCs while separating later-line monotherapy from frontline combination therapy, later-line combination therapy, and post-induction maintenance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception and in 28 August 2026. ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) were searched on 28 August 2026. We constructed an arm-level dataset that recorded regimen, dose, clinical context, target, outcome definition, numerator, denominator, analysis set, and source. The primary quantitative synthesis was restricted to second-line or later ADC monotherapy; other clinical contexts were summarized descriptively. Single-arm proportions were synthesized using a binomial-normal random-intercept generalized linear mixed model on the logit scale. We reported 95% confidence intervals (CIs), between-study variance, heterogeneity, and 95% prediction intervals. An inverse-variance logit random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp inference was used as a sensitivity analysis. Fixed-time Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and inconsistently defined common adverse events were not pooled. RESULTS: 16 trial families evaluating eight ADCs across five target classes met the eligibility criteria. In the primary later-line monotherapy analysis, the pooled ORR was 25.7% (95% CI, 16.4%-37.9%), and the pooled DCR was 72.7% (95% CI, 60.7%-82.2%). The pooled incidences of grade ≥3 TEAEs and grade ≥3 TRAEs were 62.8% (95% CI, 59.6%-65.9%) and 45.5% (95% CI, 35.5%-56.0%), respectively. The prediction intervals for ORR, DCR, and grade ≥3 TRAEs were wide. Proportions observed in a new study may therefore differ substantially from the pooled estimates. Frontline combinations, later-line combinations, and maintenance therapy yielded context-specific signals but were not compared with later-line monotherapy. Target-stratified analyses were exploratory; B7-H3 and DLL3 estimates were based on small, non-comparative groups, whereas Trop-2 and SEZ6 were not pooled because fewer than three studies were available. CONCLUSIONS: Later-line ADC monotherapy showed antitumor activity but frequent clinically important toxicity, with substantial between-study variation. The evidence does not establish superiority by treatment line, regimen, agent, or molecular target; single-arm response estimates also do not demonstrate a survival benefit. Randomized, context-specific trials using harmonized efficacy and safety definitions are needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), lurbinectedin is approved for first-line maintenance treatment with atezolizumab and as monotherapy following disease progression, but prospective real-world data on its use are lacking. METHODS: Jazz EMERGE 402 was a prospective, observational, phase 4 trial (NCT04894591) that evaluated lurbinectedin for previously treated SCLC in a diverse, real-world population. The primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR). Key secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. RESULTS: As of July 17, 2025, 267 patients received ≥ 1 lurbinectedin dose. At baseline, the median age was 67 years, 52 (19%) patients had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group score ≥ 2, 67 (25%) had brain metastases, and 88 (33%) had platinum-resistant disease. ORR (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 29% (23%-36%) overall (n = 189) and 33% (25%-42%) in second-line treatment (n = 118). Patients with brain metastases had lower ORR (17% vs 32% without; odds ratio, 0.28 [95% CI: 0.10-0.76]). Median (95% CI) PFS and OS were 3.3 (2.6-4.1) and 7.6 (6.4-8.7) months. OS was shorter with platinum-resistant vs platinum-sensitive disease (5.8 vs 9.3 months; hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI: 1.17-2.28]). Eighty-eight (33%) patients had treatment-related adverse events, including anemia (8%) and neutropenia (7%); 21 (8%) discontinued treatment due to adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: In a broad, real-world population with previously treated SCLC, lurbinectedin was associated with clinically meaningful effectiveness and predictable and manageable safety. Lower ORR and OS were seen in patients with brain metastases and platinum-resistant disease, respectively.

papers.abstract_en: Lymph nodes (LNs), principal sites of antitumor immunity, may undergo immune-mediated regression; whether neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT)-induced regression indicates prognosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We aimed to establish and validate a lymph node regression grade (LNRG) system for prognostic stratification. This multicenter, retrospective cohort study analyzed 965 patients receiving PD-1-based NCIT and surgery at three Chinese tertiary cancer centers. LNRG was the ratio of summed viable tumor area to summed bed area (residual viable plus regressed preexisting tumor) across all dissected LNs. Negative LNs were assigned LNRG 0. Survival and predictive performance were assessed using Kaplan-Meier/Cox regression, time-dependent area under the curve, Brier score, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Overall, 28,882 LNs were evaluated; patients were classified as LNRG 0-4 in 385 (39.9%), 150 (15.5%), 26 (2.7%), 141 (14.6%), and 263 (27.3%), respectively. LNRG independently predicted disease-free and overall survival, with Grades 1-2 conferring the most favorable outcomes and Grade 4 the poorest. A random survival forest model incorporating LNRG, tumor regression grade, ypAJCC stage, and perineural invasion predicted 2-year disease-free survival in training and external validation cohorts. LNRG is a novel, independent prognostic indicator after NCIT.

papers.abstract_en: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are pivotal orchestrators of immune evasion, yet the functional significance of the calcineurin signaling pathway in TAM plasticity remains elusive. Analyzing TCGA Lung Cancer datasets and clinical samples, we identified PPP3CA as the major calcineurin catalytic subunit in TAMs, whose downregulation correlates with poor patient survival and tumor progression. Myeloid-specific Ppp3ca knockout in mice accelerated tumor growth, reducing anti-tumor M1-like macrophages and CD8+ T cells while enriching pro-tumor M2-like TAMs. In vitro assays confirmed that Ppp3ca deficiency impaired the polarization of TAMs toward the M1 type. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that PPP3CA-mediated regulation of TAM plasticity is dependent on the NF-κB signaling pathway, as Ppp3ca loss significantly blunted NF-κB activation. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of calcineurin using cyclosporin A (CsA) effectively recapitulated the myeloid-deficient phenotype, shifting TAMs toward a pro-tumorigenic M2 state and promoting tumor malignancy, providing an experimental explanation for the elevated cancer risk associated with clinical calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) use. Collectively, our findings identify the PPP3CA-NF-κB axis as a pivotal regulator of macrophage plasticity and provide a high-value translational basis for targeting this pathway to remodel the TME in lung cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tislelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and its effects on serum tumor markers and inflammatory cytokines. METHODS: A total of 228 advanced ESCC patients were retrospectively enrolled and divided into an observation group (tislelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin, n=114) and a control group (chemotherapy alone: nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin, n=114). Related serological indicators, T lymphocyte subsets, quality of life, short-term efficacy, pathological response, survival outcomes and adverse reactions were compared. Independent prognostic factors were analyzed via univariate and multivariate Cox regression. RESULTS: After treatment, both groups exhibited decreased levels of tumor markers, inflammatory cytokines, soluble PD-1, PD-L1, VEGF and MMP-9, with lower levels in the observation group (all P<0.05). The observation group had improved immune function, higher SF-36 scores, as well as higher objective response rate, disease control rate, and pathological response indexes (all P<0.05). Moreover, patients in the observation group had longer progression-free survival and overall survival (both P<0.05). Advanced TNM stage was an adverse prognostic factor, while combined immunochemotherapy reduced mortality risk. CONCLUSION: Tislelizumab plus the dual chemotherapy regimen can effectively reduce serum tumor markers and alleviate tumor-related inflammation, improve immune status, quality of life and survival of patients with advanced ESCC with acceptable safety, supporting its potential for broader clinical application.

papers.abstract_en: Non-SMC condensin I complex subunit G (NCAPG) is implicated in tumor progression and TGF-β pathway activation, yet its roles in oncogenesis and immune modulation within the lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) microenvironment remain largely unexplored. Here, we used bioinformatics analysis to identify key upregulated genes in LUSC and assessed the effects of NCAPG and its upstream regulator E2F transcription factor 8 (E2F8) on malignant phenotypes via gain- and loss-of-function assays in NCI-H226 and NCI-H1703 LUSC cell lines, with in vivo efficacy validated using KLN205 cell isografts and NTCU-induced primary LUSC mouse models. Neutrophil polarization, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and CD8⁺ T cell cytotoxicity was analyzed in co-culture systems and tumor tissues. Arundanine was identified as a potential NCAPG inhibitor via molecular docking and tested as monotherapy or in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy. We found that NCAPG was significantly upregulated in LUSC, and NCAPG depletion markedly impaired LUSC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. Mechanistically, NCAPG activated TGF-β signaling, which drove pro-tumor N2 neutrophil polarization and induced NETosis; these NETs upregulated PD-L1 expression on tumor cells and suppressed the expansion and cytotoxic function of CD8⁺ T cells. E2F8 was found to transcriptionally activate NCAPG by directly binding to its promoter. Furthermore, Arundanine destabilized NCAPG protein, suppressed TGF-β-mediated NET formation, and potentiated anti-PD-1 therapy to significantly prolong survival in LUSC models. Collectively, the E2F8/NCAPG axis promotes LUSC progression by orchestrating a TGF-β-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment, and targeting NCAPG with Arundanine represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion and sensitize LUSC to PD-1 blockade.

papers.abstract_en: Anti-angiogenic therapies provide clinically meaningful benefit in selected treatment settings for advanced non-small cell lung cancer, but durable responses are limited by heterogeneous and adaptive resistance. This resistance is not solely tumor-intrinsic; it emerges from interactions among tumor plasticity, compensatory angiogenic signaling, hypoxia, stromal and immune remodeling, vascular recovery, and alternative blood-supply mechanisms. These processes require different biological variables and therefore cannot be adequately interrogated by a single experimental model. Patient-derived lung cancer organoids preserve patient-specific tumor features and are useful for studying tumor-intrinsic responses, but tumor-only organoids do not reproduce perfusion-dependent vascular physiology, permeability, or drug-delivery dynamics. Microenvironment-integrated co-culture, vascularization, and microfluidic or perfusion engineering can extend these capabilities, although model complexity alone does not establish stronger evidence. This review integrates the clinical and mechanistic basis of anti-angiogenic resistance with the capabilities and limitations of current lung cancer organoid models and other three-dimensional systems. We propose a mechanism-matched framework linking the resistance mechanism to the required variable, the minimum set of model capabilities, and claim-matched readouts. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing structural from functional vascularization, tumor drug response from anti-angiogenic resistance, and acute treatment effects from acquired resistance. Current lung cancer organoid systems can model tumor-intrinsic and selected microenvironment-mediated responses and, increasingly, vascular responses, but direct longitudinal evidence of acquired anti-angiogenic resistance remains limited. Future progress will depend on fit-for-purpose standardization, functional qualification, longitudinal modeling, and prospective alignment with clinically observed resistance trajectories.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature has been associated with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but evidence on seasonal lag patterns and susceptible populations remains limited. We characterized lag-specific and cumulative temperature-AECOPD associations during cold and warm seasons. METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (2006-2019), we conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study with referent days matched by year, season, and day of the week. Cold-season exposure was defined as 2-m air temperature (November-April), and warm-season exposure as wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT; May-October). Conditional quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models estimated lag-specific and cumulative relative risks (RRs) over 0-28 days, adjusting for season-specific meteorological variables, PM10, PM2.5, and public holidays. Effect modification by age, sex, smoking, and body mass index (BMI) was examined. RESULTS: Among 5981 AECOPD events, lower cold-season temperatures were associated with delayed, sustained risk increases over lag days 6-23, peaking at lag 14-18 (RR = 1.23; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04-1.46). Higher warm-season WBGTs were associated with an immediate increase, peaking at lag 0-1 (RR = 1.06; 95% CI 1.02-1.10), which attenuated within 1 week. Cumulative exposure-response curves were monotonic for cold-season temperature and inverted U-shaped for warm-season WBGT. Associations were stronger in men, older adults, smokers, and those with a BMI ≥25. CONCLUSION: Cold- and warm-season ambient temperature metrics showed distinct temporal associations with AECOPD, delayed in the cold season and immediate in the warm season. Associations appeared relatively stronger among older adults, men, smokers, and individuals with higher BMI.

papers.abstract_en: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are emerging therapeutic options for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after the development of resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs). However, the founding EGFR alteration alone does not guide ADC selection. At progression, actionable resistance mechanisms, altered antigen expression, central nervous system (CNS) involvement, spatial heterogeneity, and histological transformation may shift treatment priorities. This narrative review links agent-specific evidence boundaries to an eight-domain assessment of the post-progression disease state and distinguishes ADC eligibility from therapeutic priority. The framework first identifies clinical scenarios requiring immediate local, CNS-directed, or lineage-specific treatment. It then evaluates resistance-directed therapy and other systemic options in the context of prior treatment. Finally, each ADC is assessed according to its evidence base, biomarkers, construct fit, disease distribution, availability, and patient-specific safety. Currently, selected TROP2-directed ADCs have the most mature evidence. HER3-directed therapy remains under investigation, whereas c-Met- and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-directed ADCs may be relevant in biomarker-defined settings. Tissue biopsy, plasma circulating tumor DNA analysis, and selected cerebrospinal fluid testing should be considered when the findings could alter clinical management. Accordingly, ADCs should be positioned relative to competing local and systemic strategies rather than considered a uniform post-osimertinib class. Prospective validation is required to determine whether this framework improves treatment outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The acute inpatient symptom state following oesophagectomy is multidimensional and heterogeneous. However, the structure, between-patient heterogeneity, and network features of symptoms remain incompletely characterised. METHOD: We analysed 1047 postoperative patients with oesophageal cancer from four hospitals in Anhui Province, China, in the "Be Resilient to Oesophageal Cancer" program. Symptom networks were estimated and centrality computed to identify candidate targets. We then performed in silico node-perturbation simulations to estimate potential system-level effects of alleviating versus aggravating individual symptoms. RESULTS: Four symptom dimensions emerged from the principal component analysis: somatic discomfort and fatigue, psychological distress, social functioning impairment, and gastrointestinal/appetite-related symptoms. A low-burden group (80.2%) and a high-burden group (19.8%) were identified. The overall network's most central symptom was "reduced social interaction" (r = 2.52). Within groups, "worry" was most central in the low-burden group (r = 2.08), whereas "incision pain" was most central in the high-burden group (r=2.56). Computer simulations revealed that, within alleviating interventions, somatic symptoms accounted for the highest proportion across all symptom types (incision pain: -20.68% to -9.17%). Conversely, within aggravating interventions, psychosocial symptoms constituted the largest share in both the overall symptom network and the low-burden group (helplessness: 24.13% to 30.27%), whereas somatic symptoms dominated the high-burden group (incision pain: 9.17%). CONCLUSION: A multimethod pipeline identified reduced social interaction, worry, and incision pain as profile-specific, structurally prominent symptoms within the postoperative day 3 symptom networks. These findings highlight distinct psychosocial and somatic features across symptom-burden profiles and provide hypotheses for subsequent longitudinal and interventional studies.

Classification can be challenging due to overlapping histological features. Subtyping on biopsy specimens is often inaccurate due to tumor heterogeneity and sampling effect. Since 2012 an international thymic tumor pathology expert panel is available in the Netherlands. This study evaluates the added value of this panel by assessing the discrepancies in diagnosis, inter-observer agreement and concordance on diagnosis between biopsy and the subsequent resection specimen. METHODS: All pathology excerpts from 2012 until 2024 for patients diagnosed with a thymic tumor were extracted from the national PALGA database and evaluated for histological subtype, assessment and the thymoma panel result. RESULTS: In total 1163 resection and 304 biopsy specimens were included, of which 36.1% were submitted to the thymoma panel. The diagnosis changed in 15.7% of cases after assessment. The subtypes AB and Bmix were most often submitted to the thymoma panel and the diagnosis changed most often for subtype A, B3 or Bmix. In 72.8% the concordance between the panel members exceeded 90%. The biopsy diagnosis varied from the resection diagnosis in 46.8%, but the differentiation between thymoma and thymic carcinoma was accurate on biopsy. CONCLUSION: A panel of dedicated pathologists with experience in thymic abnormalities contributed substantially to a more accurate classification of TETs, thereby guiding optimal treatment planning and prognostic evaluation. Despite the discrepancies between biopsy and resection specimens, distinguishing thymoma from thymic carcinoma was accurate on biopsy.

papers.abstract_en: Radioresistance severely compromises radiotherapy efficacy for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the intrinsic heterogeneity of cellular radioresponses among isogenic tumor cells remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing (scATAC-seq) to dissect the transcriptional and regulatory landscape underlying heterogeneous radioresponses in single-cell-derived LUAD cells following 6 Gy γ-ray irradiation. We found that isogenic LUAD cells harbored intrinsic molecular determinants for divergent radiosensitivity and displayed heterogeneous radioresponsiveness upon irradiation. A radiation-associated transcriptional cell state, coupled with DNA damage repair, apoptosis, and cell cycle regulation, emerged at 6 h post-irradiation. Inhibition of lysine demethylase 4B (KDM4B) enhanced LUAD radiosensitivity by intensifying DNA damage, whereas reduced expression of cyclin B1 (CCNB1) and DNA topoisomerase IIα (TOP2A) potentially contributed to radiation-triggered G2/M arrest. Notably, the radiation-associated regulatory cell state emerged earlier than radiation-induced transcriptional cell state. RNA polymerase II subunit A (POLR2A) functioned as a core regulator in high-responsive LUAD cells. Based on these findings, we proposed a hypothesis for the radiosensitization of LUAD cells. Collectively, this study provides multilayer mechanistic insights into LUAD radioresponse heterogeneity and yields actionable molecular candidates for developing improved radiosensitization strategies to advance precise radiotherapy for LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Phase 3 evidence for antifibrotic-directed therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) has expanded, but direct head-to-head trials are lacking. Forced vital capacity (FVC) decline remains the principal trial outcome, although it may not fully capture clinically relevant differences among therapies. METHODS: We systematically reviewed phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials of antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. FVC effects versus placebo were descriptively summarized using standardized 48-52-week estimates. All-cause treatment discontinuation and all-cause mortality were analyzed using placebo-controlled odds ratios. Sensitivity analyses assessed follow-up duration, background antifibrotic therapy, and trial-level consistency. RESULTS: Ten trials including 5,386 randomized participants were included. Pirfenidone and nintedanib showed consistent reductions in FVC decline versus placebo. Inhaled treprostinil showed a favorable FVC signal in the combined TETON-1/2 evidence, largely as add-on therapy with background antifibrotic treatment. Without background antifibrotic therapy, several therapies showed directionally favorable but imprecise FVC effects, without evidence of equivalence. Nintedanib and inhaled treprostinil were associated with higher odds of all-cause treatment discontinuation versus placebo: OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.02-1.88) and OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.08-1.78), respectively. Pirfenidone was the only therapy associated with lower odds of all-cause mortality (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.31-0.83), based on published pooled ASCEND/CAPACITY mortality data and the Japanese phase 3 trial. CONCLUSIONS: FVC decline remains essential but may not fully distinguish antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. Integrating FVC effects, background therapy, treatment continuation, and mortality provides a cautious, context-dependent framework for interpreting expanding phase 3 evidence.

papers.abstract_en: Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the epigenetic mechanisms underlying platinum resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that Jumonji C domain-containing protein 5 (JMJD5) promotes platinum resistance in NSCLC cells and xenograft tumors while inducing a slow-proliferative, mesenchymal-like phenotype characterized by enhanced migration, invasion, spheroid formation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Mechanistically, JMJD5 interacted with RCC1 domain-containing protein 1 (RCCD1), and cisplatin treatment promoted their nuclear accumulation concomitant with reduced H3K36me2 levels. RCCD1 depletion attenuated JMJD5-associated H3K36me2 demethylation and reversed EMT-associated phenotypes and cisplatin resistance, supporting RCCD1 as a functional cofactor of JMJD5-mediated chromatin remodeling. Fibronectin 1 (FN1) was further identified as a downstream effector of this pathway. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of FN1 suppressed JMJD5-induced migration and invasion and restored cisplatin sensitivity. Notably, JMJD5-dependent FN1 protein accumulation required ongoing protein synthesis without a corresponding increase in FN1 mRNA, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation. Consistently, elevated FN1 expression was associated with unfavorable overall survival in patients with lung cancer. Collectively, these findings reveal a JMJD5-RCCD1-H3K36me2-FN1 regulatory axis linking chemotherapy-induced epigenetic remodeling to EMT-associated platinum resistance and suggest that disruption of this pathway may represent a potential strategy for overcoming chemoresistance in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have transformed the treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), yet durable responses remain limited to a minority of patients. Tumor plasticity is increasingly recognized as a determinant of immunotherapy resistance, although the tumor-intrinsic contribution of immunomodulatory mediators such as IFN-γ and PD-L1 remains poorly understood. In this review, we examine emerging evidence that IFN-γ and PD-L1, beyond their established roles in tumor-immune interactions, may contribute to the regulation of NSCLC plasticity. IFN-γ can activate non-canonical programs involving dose-dependent ICAM1/PI3K/AKT/Notch1 signaling, BCAT1- and FGF2/β-catenin-mediated metabolic reprogramming, and a putative autocrine TBX21/IL-4 signaling circuit that may sustain stem-like properties. PD-L1, in turn, is functionally integrated into plasticity-associated pathways involving the TGF-β signaling axis, β-catenin stabilization, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-associated microRNA networks, YAP/TAZ, CD44 and ATM signaling, as well as TRAF6/BECN1/NF-κB-dependent regulation of autophagy. Collectively, these findings support a role for IFN-γ and PD-L1 as context-dependent modulators of NSCLC plasticity, with potential implications for immunotherapy resistance, and provide a rationale for further exploring combinatorial treatment strategies and patient stratification approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Golgin-45 (G45) is a coiled-coil protein that transits reversibly between the Golgi and nucleus. In the Golgi, G45 serves as a tether for effectors of a pro-tumorigenic secretory program, but its nuclear role remains unclear. Here, we report that, upon entering the nucleus, G45 functions as a basic leucine zipper transcription factor. From genomic mapping, RNA-sequencing, and functional validation studies, we identify G45-binding sites and show that nuclear G45 can function as a transcriptional activator or repressor, a versatility enabled by phase separation into nuclear bodies enriched in transcriptional co-regulators. In lung cancer models, Golgi-docking reinforces, whereas nuclear translocation opposes, pro-tumorigenic activity of G45. Nuclear G45 incorporates into dimeric transcription factors that silence pro-tumorigenic secreted cargos. Epigenetic events in lung cancer degrade nuclear G45 and sequester G45 in the Golgi, which unleashes malignant secretion. Thus, inter-organelle transitions govern a G45-dependent secretory axis that drives lung cancer progression.

papers.abstract_en: To investigate the local control and safety of adding high-dose-rate intraluminal brachytherapy (HDR-ILBT) with novel balloon applicator (BRAXX) after concurrent chemoradiation (CCRT) for non-surgery patients with esophageal cancer. The study enrolled 178 patients with esophageal cancer. A total of 13 patients were prospectively recruited to receive HDR-ILBT after CCRT and compared with two standard-of-care cohorts treated between 2022 and 2024. Brachytherapy was delivered via the BRAXX balloon applicator (Taiwan Food and Drug Administration approval No. 006603) using an Iridium-192 Nucletron remote afterloading system (Elekta, Stockholm, Sweden). The primary endpoint was freedom from local tumor recurrence (FFLTR). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), disease progression-free survival (DPFS), and toxicities. Sankey diagrams and swimmer plot were utilized to visualize the longitudinal tumor response dynamics and individual survival trajectories. The median follow-up was 25.2 months. The 1-year and 2-year FFLTR rates were 93.3% and 81.2% (nCCRT + surgery), 84.6% and 67.7% (CCRT + ILBT), and 62.5% and 52.9% (dCCRT alone), respectively (P < 0.001). Consistent survival improvements were observed in both OS and DPFS in CCRT + ILBT cohort. Sankey diagrams demonstrated a favorable dynamic evolution in treatment response within the CCRT + ILBT cohort, achieving a clinical complete response (cCR) rate of 61.5% and overall response rate (ORR) of 69.2% at the end of per-protocol 1-year follow-up. Swimmer plot illustrated that response conversion and consolidation translated into long-term survival. The addition of HDR-ILBT did not exacerbate treatment-related esophageal strictures or fistula formations necessitating intervention. The addition of HDR-ILBT utilizing BRAXX applicator following CCRT is a feasible and promising strategy to enhance local control and prolong survival for non-surgical patients with esophageal cancer. By leveraging its distinct dosimetric advantages and streamlined workflow, ILBT holds the potential to consolidate disease-free status and eradicate residual disease. Further validation through large-scale, prospective clinical trials is still warranted to confirm its clinical benefit and long-term safety. If further validated, this strategy could offer a meaningful addition to the current treatment paradigm.

papers.abstract_en: Although single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy is increasingly adopted for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evidence comparing its long-term oncological efficacy with that of the two-port approach remains scarce. This propensity score-matched study evaluated perioperative outcomes, postoperative recovery, and 3-year survival following single-port versus two-port thoracoscopic lobectomy in patients with NSCLC. We retrospectively analyzed 167 consecutive patients (single-port, n = 82; two-port, n = 85); propensity score matching (1:1, caliper = 0.2) yielded 72 matched pairs. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative pain (VAS), inflammatory markers (CRP, PCT, IL-1β), pulmonary function, 30-day complications, 3-year overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and multivariable Cox regression were compared. Following matching, the single-port group demonstrated significantly longer operative time (187.3 ± 56.4 vs. 142.2 ± 49.4 minutes; P<0.001) but reduced blood loss (96.5 ± 42.0 vs. 121.7 ± 48.1 mL; P<0.001) 24-hour chest drainage volume (632.3 ± 447.3 vs. 945.5 ± 501.3 mL; P<0.001), and incision length (3.57 ± 1.37 vs. 4.94 ± 1.52 cm; P<0.001). Lymph node yield did not differ significantly (17.3 ± 4.1 vs. 16.1 ± 3.6; P = 0.058). Postoperative VAS scores were significantly lower in the single-port group on days 3, 5, and 7 (all P<0.001), with attenuated inflammatory responses (lower CRP, PCT, and IL-1β; all P<0.001) and better pulmonary function recovery (higher PaO2, SpO2, FVC, and FEV1; all P<0.05). Thirty-day complication rates did not differ significantly (6.9% vs. 9.7%; P = 0.763). Over a median follow-up of 38 months, 3-year OS (86.5% vs. 84.4%; P = 0.572) and 3-year DFS (79.2% vs. 77.1%; P = 0.684) were comparable. Multivariable analysis identified pathological stage II (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.35-4.43; P = 0.003) and lymphovascular invasion (HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.18-3.72; P = 0.012) as independent predictors of poorer DFS, whereas surgical approach was not associated with DFS or OS. In conclusion, single-port thoracoscopic lobectomy was associated with reduced surgical trauma, decreased postoperative pain and inflammation, and improved pulmonary function recovery, without compromising lymph node dissection, short-term safety, or 3-year oncological outcomes. These findings support the continued use and wider adoption of single-port VATS in appropriately selected patients with NSCLC, while acknowledging that Stage I disease predominance limits generalizability to more advanced stages.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose To assess pulmonary gas exchange in participants with cystic fibrosis (CF) relative to control participants, evaluate the effect of CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy, and assess subclinical lung disease using xenon 129 (129Xe) MRI. Materials and Methods Participants with CF and control participants were prospectively enrolled between October 2019 and February 2024 and underwent 129Xe MRI and spirometry. Images from gaseous xenon, xenon dissolved in pulmonary capillary red blood cells (RBCs), and dissolved in the gas-exchange membrane (interstitial tissue and capillary plasma) were binned into three compartments to generate maps of ventilation, RBC transfer, and membrane uptake. Spirometric and imaging differences between participants with CF and control participants were assessed using analysis of variance with Tukey post hoc corrections, and associations were analyzed using Kendall rank correlation. Results Sixty-one participants with CF (median age, 14.2 years; IQR, 10.0-19.7 years; 33 female) and 47 controls (median age, 24.9 years; IQR, 20.9-29.2 years; 25 males) were included. For participants with CF, spirometry (percent predicted) was normal: forced expiratory volume after 1 second (median, 98.2%; IQR, 87.2%-109%), forced vital capacity (median, 104%; IQR, 96.8%-112%), and forced expiratory flow between 25% and 75% forced vital capacity (median, 88.1%; IQR, 69.9%-108%). Membrane uptake correlated with elevated RBC transfer (τ = 0.62; P < .001) for participants with CF on and off CFTR modulator therapy. Conclusion Participants with CF had higher RBC transfer and membrane uptake than control participants. Membrane uptake was elevated in participants with CF exhibiting normal spirometry and receiving highly effective CFTR modulator therapy. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans. METHODS: A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection. RESULTS: Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

papers.abstract_en: Although multi-hit TP53 mutations correlate with rapid disease progression, treatment resistance, recurrence, and poor survival, their occurrence within an individual TP53 gene molecule (cbTP53) remains unexplored. Consequently, the impact of cbTP53 on protein conformation, transcriptional architecture, and oncogenicity is unknown. We show that cbTP53 with combined mutations (Y220C+R248Q+R282Q) does not drastically alter local stability or structural conformation, but significantly affects TP53 binding to DNA promoters comparing it to a single Y220C mutation. Functionally, cbTP53 promotes divergent cellular phenotypes, characterized by enhanced cell proliferation, increased formation of multicellular tumor spheroids (MCTS) and spheroids, altered responses to chemotherapeutic drugs (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin) and p53 inhibitors (e.g., MB710, PK11007), and increased resistance to carboplatin-induced DNA damage. Furthermore, cbTP53 is linked to distinct immune cell profiles (e.g., CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, nature killer cells, dendritic cells), more circulating tumor cells, a higher rate of tumor engraftment, and an increased number of lung tumor nodules. Mechanistically, introduction of R248Q/R282Q mutations changes 42.7% of Y220C-regulated gene expression, and cbTP53 (vs Y220C) owns a distinctive transcriptomic signature with 1,004 up- and 1,747 down-regulated genes. cbTP53 shows the enhanced binding affinity in the promoters of inflammatory cytokines, leading to their increased production. This study establishes causative and mechanistic links of cbTP53 to lung aggressive cancer metastasis and disease progression, providing a novel perspective on the genetics of TP53 mutations in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to estimate the incidence, mortality, and overall survival (OS) of esophageal cancer (EC) and to evaluate the association of clinicopathological characteristics and treatment modality with OS. METHODS: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted using data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) in rural central India. The dataset included 545 incident EC cases registered between 2010 and 2019, of which 476 were eligible for OS analysis. Incidence and mortality rates were estimated, OS was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify prognostic factors. Prespecified sensitivity analyses, including metastasis-adjusted and age-stratified Cox regression models, were performed to assess the robustness of the primary multivariable findings. RESULTS: The age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) of overall EC cases was 3.99 per 100,000 population (95% CI: 3.50-4.47), while the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) was 3.29 per 100,000 population (95% CI: 2.94-3.64). The overall median survival was 178.33 days (95% CI: 115.49-234.48). The OS rates at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years were 31.3%, 19.7%, 17.4%, and 14.6%, respectively. OS differed significantly according to tumor site (χ² = 5.24, p = 0.043), treatment modality (χ² = 15.42, p = 0.031), and metastatic status (χ² = 162.64, p < 0.001) on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Median survival was 232 days (95% CI: 159.59-304.41) for localized disease, 199 days (95% CI: 166.38-231.61) for regional disease, 68 days (95% CI: 54.21-81.79) for distant disease, and 28 days (95% CI: 15.56-40.44) for advanced disease. On univariable Cox regression, patients with middle-third tumors had a lower hazard of death than those with upper-third tumors (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.56-0.98; p = 0.036), and this remained significant after adjustment for metastatic status and in the age-stratified sensitivity model, while metastatic disease was associated with progressively higher mortality. Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy and surgery plus chemotherapy were independently associated with lower mortality after multivariable adjustment (HR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.28-0.85, p = 0.011; HR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.21-0.94, p = 0.035, respectively). Age, sex, and histological type were not significantly associated with OS. CONCLUSION: EC demonstrated a substantial mortality burden and poor OS in this population-based cohort. Metastatic status was the strongest associated prognostic factor, while tumor site and treatment modality were associated with survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy and surgery plus chemotherapy remained independently associated with lower mortality after multivariable adjustment. These findings highlight the importance of early diagnosis, accurate assessment of disease extent, and appropriate multimodal management of EC.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pleural effusion remains diagnostically challenging when standard thoracentesis does not establish an aetiology. This pilot analysis described sequential biomarker measurements in patients proceeding to medical thoracoscopy and explored their associations and discrimination across final diagnostic classifications. METHODS: Prospectively collected data from a single-centre tertiary referral cohort were analysed. Pleural-fluid adenosine deaminase (ADA) and serum complement components 3 and 4 (C3 and C4) were obtained on day 1, whereas pleural-fluid cancer antigen 125 (CA125) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were obtained at the day 7/thoracoscopy evaluation. Final classifications were based on a composite reference standard integrating thoracoscopy, histopathology, microbiology, cytology, imaging, and clinical follow-up. Analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: Amongst 75 patients, 6 (8.0%) were classified as tuberculous pleural effusion (TB-PE), 33 (44.0%) as malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and 36 (48.0%) as other non-tuberculous, non-malignant pleural effusions. ADA differed across groups (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.002; Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.010) and showed exploratory discrimination for TB-PE (area under the curve [AUC] 0.934; bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.855-0.995). CA125, LDH, C3 and C4 did not show significant omnibus group differences after reanalysis. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding 26 patients retained as non-specific pleuritis (n = 49), ADA remained significantly different across groups (P = 0.004; q = 0.022). CONCLUSIONS: In this selected thoracoscopy cohort, day 1 pleural-fluid ADA showed the clearest exploratory signal, including after exclusion of non-specific pleuritis, but estimates were based on only six TB-PE cases and do not establish stand-alone utility or a role in avoiding thoracoscopy.
