papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, including among patients diagnosed with potentially curable disease. Current decisions regarding perioperative treatment and follow-up rely on a limited number of established prognostic factors. Further knowledge is needed regarding the clinical, histopathological, and molecular factors associated with subsequent metastatic disease, particularly brain metastasis (BM), which is associated with poor prognosis. We investigated these factors in a large cohort of patients with surgically resected stage I-III lung cancer followed for more than five years. BM was associated with higher pathological tumour and lymph-node stage and younger age at surgery. Lung adenocarcinoma was associated with a higher risk of BM than lung squamous cell carcinoma. Several molecular alterations were associated with metastatic disease or BM, including KRAS mutations in lung adenocarcinoma and NFE2L2 mutations in lung squamous cell carcinoma. Additional associations involving specific EGFR and KRAS mutation subtypes and rarer alterations were observed, but were based on small numbers of cases and should be considered exploratory. Several of the associated genes are involved in the RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, or NRF2-related pathways. However, pathway activation and causality could not be established in this observational study. These findings support further investigation of clinical, histopathological, and molecular factors associated with metastatic progression after surgical resection. Validation in larger, independent, stage-stratified and contemporary cohorts with comprehensive treatment data is required before the identified molecular alterations can be considered for clinical risk stratification or surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality despite major therapeutic advances. Precision oncology has revolutionized the management of LUAD by identifying actionable molecular biomarkers and developing targeted therapies. In this review, we summarize the major predictive biomarkers in LUAD, including EGFR, KRAS, ALK, ROS1, MET, RET, BRAF, HER2, NTRK, and PD-L1, and describe the currently approved targeted therapies and emerging therapeutic strategies. Recent advances in selective inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and immune checkpoint inhibitors that have improved clinical outcomes in molecularly defined patient populations are highlighted. The review also discusses the molecular basis of acquired resistance, such as on-target mutations, bypass signalling activation, histological transformation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition that continue to limit long-term therapeutic efficacy. We also discuss emerging strategies to overcome resistance, including combination therapies, next-generation inhibitors, liquid biopsy-guided monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted precision medicine. Collectively, these findings highlight the need for comprehensive molecular characterization and integrated biomarker-guided treatment strategies to improve therapeutic decision-making and clinical outcomes in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Approximately 2% of lung tumours are pulmonary carcinoids (PCs), divided into typical (90%) and atypical (AC) (10%). The link with external exposure to carcinogens remains controversial. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between occupational exposure to carcinogens and PC tumours. METHODS: A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review was performed. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Embase (January 2025). Studies were reviewed, data extracted, analysed and summarised narratively. RESULTS: 1302 studies were reviewed. 27 original studies and seven conference papers on topics including exposure to cigarette smoke (n=23) and asbestos (n=6), or mechanistic information, were included. Following the collapse of the World Trade Center in 2001, carcinoids accounted for 6% of lung cancer cases in people exposed to the resulting dust (9% in women, 3% in men). The proportion of ACs among carcinoids rose from 9.3% (controls) to 16.3% (smokers) and from ∼25% to 45% (probable versus definite asbestos exposure). Basic research has identified biological pathways linking harmful exposures (such as asbestos and cigarette smoke) to neuroendocrine cell proliferation and the potential progression of PCs to higher-grade lung tumours. DISCUSSION: The significance these of findings is limited due to 1) the limited number of studies, 2) the small number of tumours within those studies and 3) the lack of rigid diagnostic (morphological and molecular) criteria for PCs in most studies. Nevertheless, a consistent finding is a higher proportion of AC among carcinoids, particularly following asbestos exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Based on these findings, a link between carcinogenic substances (especially asbestos and cigarette smoke) and carcinoids seems plausible. More stringent analyses in epidemiological surveys are needed to further clarify the pathogenesis of PCs.

papers.abstract_en: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutant-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) frequently develops acquired resistance to third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), particularly through the EGFR C797S mutation. Existing EGFR-targeting proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remain limited by unfavorable pharmacokinetics and suboptimal selectivity inherited from their parent TKIs. To address these limitations, we developed HQY1480, a next-generation PROTAC derived from the macrocyclic fourth-generation EGFR inhibitor BI-4020. Systematic linker and E3 ligase ligand optimization enabled potent and selective degradation of multiple clinically relevant EGFR mutants with single-digit nanomolar DC50 values. HQY1480 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, stronger suppression of oncogenic signaling than BI-4020, and no detectable off-target degradation in proteomic profiling. In xenograft models, HQY1480 outperformed BI-4020, overcame osimertinib resistance, and effectively inhibited tumor growth at low doses, while inducing robust EGFR degradation in patient-derived xenografts. These findings establish HQY1480 as an effective and well-tolerated lead PROTAC for EGFR-mutant NSCLC with acquired resistance to third-generation TKIs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema-associated pulmonary hypertension (CPFE-PH) has emerged as a distinct third category of PH, yet its detailed clinical-hemodynamic profile, pathological features, and comparative outcomes remain poorly defined. This study aims to characterize the phenotype of CPFE-PH and compare it with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease-related PH (COPD-PH) and idiopathic interstitial pneumonia-related PH (IIP-PH). METHODS: In this multicenter cohort study, we analyzed 113 patients with CPFE-PH, 277 with COPD-PH, and 78 with IIP-PH, all diagnosed by right heart catheterization. Clinical, physiological, imaging, pathological, treatment response, and survival data were statistically compared across groups. RESULTS: CPFE-PH patients were older, predominantly male smokers, and exhibited preserved ventilatory function but severely reduced diffusing capacity (DLCO 31.6% predicted, IQR 24.8-37.8). They had the most severe hemodynamic compromise (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 41 mmHg, pulmonary vascular resistance 7.4 Wood units), a high prevalence of mediastinal lymphadenopathy (81.4%), and universal capillary hemangiomatosis-like remodeling, a pathological feature absent in COPD-PH and rarely observed in IIP-PH. Pulmonary arterial hypertension-targeted therapy failed to improve functional or biomarker outcomes, and transplant-free survival was shortest in CPFE-PH (median 32 months) compared with COPD-PH and IIP-PH (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: CPFE-PH appears to represent a severe phenotype within Group 3 PH, in which prominent capillary remodeling, including hemangiomatosis-like changes, may contribute to its clinical, radiological, and functional manifestations, distinguish it from other Group 3 PH types. papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram based on clinical and computed tomography (CT) features for the preoperative prediction of invasiveness in patients with solitary pulmonary ground-glass nodules (GGNs). We retrospectively analyzed 846 patients with solitary GGNs who underwent surgical resection at the Lung Cancer Center of West China Hospital between November 2022 and January 2024. All nodules were pathologically confirmed as atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (AAH), adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA), or invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC). Patients were classified into a non-invasive group (including AAH, AIS, and MIA) and an IAC group based on postoperative pathological results. Clinical data and CT features before surgery were collected. Patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 592) and a validation cohort (n = 254) in a ratio of 7:3. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, followed by multivariate logistic regression to identify independent predictors and construct a nomogram model. The variance inflation factor (VIF) was used to evaluate multicollinearity among the candidate predictors. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that the maximum tumor diameter (OR = 39.82, 95% CI: 16.29-97.32), consolidation-to-tumor ratio (0.5<CTR<1, OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.36-4.63), vacuole sign (OR = 2.29, 95% CI: 1.29-4.07), pleura traction sign (OR = 3.03, 95% CI: 1.66-5.53), and the presence of solid component on the mediastinal window (OR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.46-7.28) were independent risk factors for IAC. The nomogram constructed based on these variables demonstrated good discriminative ability, with AUC values of 0.930 and 0.913 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between the predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA indicated favorable clinical utility. Consequently, this nomogram based on the maximum tumor diameter, CTR, vacuole sign, pleura traction sign, and the presence of solid component on the mediastinal window, provides an effective and noninvasive tool for preoperative prediction of the invasiveness of solitary GGNs.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: To summarize the clinical features, treatment patterns and survival outcomes of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) combined with connective tissue disease (CTD), and to determine whether CTD independently influences prognosis and treatment-related toxicity in this special patient population. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we enrolled 200 consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed NSCLC. Among them, 95 patients met the diagnostic criteria for CTD were set as the CTD group, and the remaining 105 patients with simple NSCLC as the control group. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), baseline tumor characteristics, metastatic patterns, first-line treatment patterns and delivery, and treatment-related adverse events (AEs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the prognostic effect of CTD and identify independent survival predictors. Meanwhile, the CTD group had higher risks of chemotherapy dose reduction (P = 0.011), treatment delay longer than 7 days (P = 0.015) and early treatment discontinuation (P = 0.002). In survival outcomes, the median PFS was 5.4 vs 7.8 months (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.17-2.13; P = 0.003), and the median OS was 9.7 vs 14.6 months (HR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.29-2.40; P<0.001). Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that CTD was an independent adverse prognostic factor for poor OS (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.01-1.97; P = 0.044). CONCLUSION: For patients diagnosed with NSCLC, comorbid CTD is correlated with aggravated intrathoracic tumor dissemination, reduced treatment intensity and treatment tolerance, increased severe toxicity, and dismal long-term survival.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: ORCHARD (NCT03944772) was a biomarker-directed, phase II, platform study conducted to characterize resistance mechanisms and evaluate novel treatment combinations in patients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on first-line osimertinib. papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Virtual-assisted lung mapping (VAL-MAP) is a safe and useful procedure for identifying suitable lines for sublobar lung resections. RESULTS: Overall, 178 preoperative markings (75 patients) were included: 74 markings in 35 patients in the UTB VAL-MAP group and 104 markings in 40 patients in the conventional VAL-MAP group. Furthermore, the marking success rate using indigo carmine in the UTB VAL-MAP group was higher for lesions located in the upper lobe and S6 region than that in the conventional VAL-MAP group (P < 0.001). In multivariate generalized estimating equations models, UTB use (odds ratio = 7.390, P = 0.015) was significantly associated with overall detection rate. No severe procedure-related complications occurred in either group. CONCLUSION: UTB VAL-MAP appears useful for increasing the rate of successful visceral pleura marking, particularly in the upper lobes or S6 areas, which the conventional VAL-MAP technique has difficulty reaching, without increasing complications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: De novo malignancies are a major cause of late death following lung transplantation (LTx). Although previous reports from Japan have identified post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) as the most common de novo malignancy, comprehensive long-term data on the spectrum, treatment, and outcomes of de novo malignancies remain limited. RESULTS: De novo malignancy was diagnosed in 53 patients (12.8%), comprising 18 cases of PTLD and 37 cases of solid tumors (42 tumors in total). The cumulative incidence of PTLD was 3.1% at 1 year and remained stable thereafter, whereas the incidence of solid tumors increased steadily over time, reaching 16.8% at 10 years after LTx. PTLD and solid tumors showed distinct temporal patterns, with median times to onset of 8.0 months and 64.0 months, respectively. Regarding post-LTx lung cancer, five of the six cases (83.3%) originated in the native lung after single LTx. The 2-year overall survival after malignancy diagnosis was significantly higher in the curative treatment group than in the non-curative group (87.9% vs. 16.7%, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that the risk of solid malignancies continues to increase during long-term follow-up after LTx. The favorable outcomes observed among patients receiving curative treatment are considered to reflect earlier detection and better baseline patients' condition, underscoring the importance of post-transplant cancer surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: In September 2021, the eruption of the Tajogaite volcano on La Palma (Spain) released large amounts of toxic gases and particulate matter over three months. This study, part of the ASHES Project, analyses the serum cytokine profile and its relationship with exposure to these pollutants in general population, asthma patients, and occupationally exposed workers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 102 participants (69 women; median age 50 years) were included. Structured interviews were conducted, and serum samples were collected to quantify 48 biomarkers related to TH1, TH2, and TH17 inflammatory responses (Olink®). Participants were classified into three groups: healthy population (n = 66), occupationally exposed workers (n = 13), and asthmatic patients (n = 23). Comparisons were performed between healthy population vs. asthmatics and healthy population vs. occupational group. RESULTS: Occupationally exposed workers showed the highest exposure (median 10 h), compared with 6 h in the healthy population and 5 h in asthmatics (p = 0.006). This group, with highest exposure, had increased levels of IL-2, IL-7, IL-17A, and IL-17F compared with the general population. Asthmatic patients showed higher levels of IL-2, IL-7, TNFSF12, CXCL10, IL-17C, CCL3, and CCL4, and lower levels of IL-15 and MMP12 (p < 0.05). A strong positive correlation between IL-4 and exposure time (r = 0.7935, p < 0.0001), and negative correlations with CCL8, CXCL11, and TNF-α were observed in asthmatics. CONCLUSIONS: Volcanic emissions are associated with exposure- and disease-dependent immune responses. Asthmatics show heightened TH1/TH2/TH17 activation, while highly exposed workers display a TH17-skewed profile, with the general population maintaining a balanced response, suggesting greater vulnerability in asthma patients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thoracic cancers during pregnancy are rare but increasingly encountered because of delayed childbearing and the rising incidence of cancer in younger individuals. Despite guideline recommendations, exposure to targeted small-molecule therapies occurs across all trimesters, but safety data remain limited. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the safety of targeted small-molecule therapies for thoracic cancers during pregnancy by combining VigiBase data with a systematic review. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We performed a pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis based on the reporting odds ratio (ROR) and a systematic review. Individual case safety reports from VigiBase (January 1, 2006-February 24, 2026) were analysed. A systematic review of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus through June 25, 2026 included case reports and case series. RESULTS: The VigiBase analysis included 15,023 reports of anticancer exposure during pregnancy, of which 162 involved small molecules currently used on- and off-label for thoracic cancers, including 75 with approved agents for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Compared with other anticancer agents, including cytotoxic drugs, immune checkpoint inhibitors, other immunotherapies, antibody-drug conjugates, molecularly targeted therapies (including biologics and small molecules other than those of interest), and anticancer agents not further specified, the small molecules of interest were associated with disproportionate reporting of premature labor (ROR: 2.64; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.21-5.75), foetal growth restriction (ROR: 2.10; 95% CI 1.15-3.84), neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (ROR: 3.78; 95% CI 1.50-9.57), and low birth weight (ROR: 2.27; 95% CI 1.18-4.37). Among approved small molecules for NSCLC, signals were observed for premature labor (ROR: 4.17; 95% CI 1.65-10.53), neonatal respiratory complications (ROR: 2.56; 95% CI 1.02-6.42), and low birth weight (ROR: 3.55; 95% CI 1.61-7.83). Of note, anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor ICSRs were fewer, and 14/18 alectinib reports described pregnancy exposure without pregnancy-related ADRs of interest, precluding alectinib-specific disproportionality analysis. The systematic review included 26 women (27 pregnancies) with oncogene-driven metastatic NSCLC. Live births occurred in 96.3% of pregnancies, with 53.8% preterm deliveries, 33.3% pregnancy complications, and 19.2% neonatal complications. Maternal outcomes were favourable (objective response rate 80.8%). There were no clinically significant pregnancy complications reported in the 10 cases involving alectinib exposure alone. CONCLUSIONS: Exposure during pregnancy to small molecules currently used on- and off-label for thoracic cancers was associated with disproportionate reporting signals for selected adverse foetal outcomes. The available clinical evidence remains limited, and although no clinically significant pregnancy complications were reported with alectinib exposure, the current data are insufficient to establish its safety. Treatment decisions should therefore be individualised and made within a multidisciplinary expert setting.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: DNA methylation alterations are stable, biologically informative, and detectable in tissue and circulating DNA, making them promising biomarkers for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, few methylation biomarkers have entered routine clinical practice. We aimed to characterize the evolution and translational challenges of this field. METHODS: Publications on NSCLC, DNA methylation, and biomarker applications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection through 31 December 2025. After PRISMA-based screening, bibliometric and knowledge-map analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 1,910 publications were included. Annual output increased after 2010 and peaked in 2022. Lung Cancer was the most productive journal, whereas Cancer Research had the highest citation impact. China contributed the largest publication volume, while the United States had the highest citation impact. Foundational studies focused on promoter hypermethylation, methylation-specific PCR, and methylated DNA detection in accessible biospecimens. Research priorities shifted from candidate-gene studies toward methylation signatures, liquid biopsy, multi-omics integration, immunotherapy-related applications, and computational modeling. CONCLUSION: NSCLC methylation biomarker research has evolved toward integrated translational frameworks. Future progress requires multicenter validation, standardized platforms, clinically defined methylation panels, and AI-assisted integration. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: High-dose-rate endobronchial brachytherapy (HDR-BTE) is an effective technique for the treatment of malignant tracheobronchial tumors. Although two-dimensional (2D) planning provides limited dosimetric information and does not accurately assess the relationship between the catheter and the tumor or the dose delivered to organs at risk (OARs), it continues to be used because it ensures adequate PTV coverage, is associated with low toxicity, and minimizes the risk of catheter displacement by avoiding patient transfer to the CT simulation room. The esophagus was the most sensitive organ, showing the highest doses in the posterior orientation of the catheter. The contralateral lung and heart received low doses; while the aorta showed higher doses in the favorable oblique scenario due to the location of the PTV. CONCLUSIONS: Catheter orientation in HDR-BTE has a significant impact on PTV coverage and the dose delivered to critical organs. Despite the trend toward 3D planning, there is no direct clinical evidence comparing the two techniques.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) targeting programmed death-1 or its ligand (PD-1/PD-L1) is being explored as an addition to standard treatment for esophageal cancer (EC) to improve response rates, yet robust methods for patient selection are lacking. CONCLUSIONS: The global disease burden of early-onset female TBL continues to increase in younger populations in low SDI regions. Ambient particulate matter pollution is the primary growth factor. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary team (MDT) review is essential for individualized treatment planning in lung cancer, where decisions often require integration of staging, pathology, molecular findings, performance status, and multimodal treatment options. However, the effective implementation of MDT review remains constrained by limited specialist availability in resource-limited hospitals and by high patient volume, heavy physician workload, and tight clinical schedules in tertiary care centers. Large language models (LLMs) may support MDT workflows by synthesizing clinical information and generating preliminary treatment recommendations for clinician review. This study compared GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro with expert MDT recommendations in real-world lung cancer cases and evaluated how information completeness and input format influenced LLM-generated treatment recommendations. METHODS: We conducted a head-to-head evaluation of GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro for lung-cancer multidisciplinary team decision support. For each of 150 consecutively collected cases, structured vignettes were entered using three information-completeness levels in both natural-language and isomorphic JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) formats. Each model produced a single-sentence recommendation. Outputs were compared with the expert multidisciplinary team plan, which was treated as a clinical reference standard for concordance analysis rather than an objective guideline-only gold standard, using predefined plan-level categories. To better quantify model performance, we applied keyword extraction and semantic matching to normalize both multidisciplinary team recommendations and model outputs into ten treatment categories with subsequent manual review and correction. RESULTS: Stratifying by information level and format, Information Level III produced the best overall performance for Gemini-2.5-Pro under natural-language input, with F1 0.7603, accuracy 0.8647, precision 0.7031, and recall 0.8278. GPT-5 achieved its highest recall under Information Level III with JSON input (recall 0.9132), but this was accompanied by lower precision and F1. Under the same natural-language Information Level III, GPT-5 reached recall 0.8770 with F1 0.6826 and accuracy 0.7967. CONCLUSIONS: Gemini-2.5-Pro show promise as adjuncts to MDT decision-making in lung cancer, offering high agreement with expert plans under controlled conditions. With appropriate clinician oversight, LLM-based tools may help expand access to standardized, high-quality recommendations where specialist availability is limited.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Physical functioning has emerged as a potentially valuable prognostic indicator in patients with nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of objectively measured components of physical functioning on survival outcomes across treatment modalities. METHODS: Medline, Web of Science and Scopus were searched up to May 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients with NSCLC and assessed at least one objectively measured physical functioning indicator in relation to survival outcomes. Indicators were categorised using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework into "body functions and structures", "activities" and "participation" and studies were stratified into "surgery" and "nonsurgery" groups. Meta-analyses were conducted when data permitted it. RESULTS: 58 studies (19 436 patients) were included. Most assessments were performed before treatment. In the surgical group, only "activities"-based measures were evaluated. A meta-analysis restricted to this group showed that survivors had substantially higher (functional) exercise capacity, measured through cardiopulmonary exercise testing and field tests (standardised mean difference 0.79). In nonsurgical cohorts, prognostic value extended across all ICF domains, with low handgrip strength (hazard ratio (HR) 1.27), low (functional) exercise capacity (HR 2.11) and physical inactivity (HR 2.86) associated with significantly higher mortality. Notably, no studies in surgical cohorts evaluated "body functions" or "participation". Heterogeneity and varying thresholds were noted across studies. CONCLUSIONS: Objectively measured physical functioning is a significant prognostic indicator of survival in NSCLC. Routine assessment could enhance risk stratification and guide personalised care. Future research should address longitudinal changes, standardisation of measures and targeted interventions.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT). METHODS: Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion. RESULTS: Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare. CONCLUSIONS: Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is one of the deadliest forms of cancer, with a significantly high mortality rate. Consequently, early diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment and improved survival outcomes. The cytokeratin 19 fragment, CYFRA 21-1, is a key biomarker for lung cancer detection and is strongly associated with non-small cell lung cancer, particularly squamous cell carcinoma. Accordingly, establishing a sensitive and reliable method for early lung cancer diagnosis based on CYFRA 21-1 detection is critical to improving clinical outcomes. This study introduces a new highly sensitive competitive electrochemical platform capable of detecting CYFRA 21-1using gold nanoparticles (AuNPs)/graphene oxide (GO)/MoO3-MoS2 nanocomposite and gold (Au) nanotags. The sensing platform is constructed by depositing CYFRA 21-1 on a AuNPs/GO/MoO3-MoS2 nanocomposite-modified screen-printed electrode (SPE). In the detection process, the electrode specifically captures unbound anti-CYFRA 21-1 on hydroquinone (HQ)@Au nanotags after competitive binding to the target CYFRA 21-1 in the sample. Our strategy for signal amplification uses the electrochemical response of HQ, anchored to nanotags, as a redox probe. The combination of three nanomaterials enhances electrode reactivity by increasing surface area and conductivity, while maintaining sufficient CYFRA 21-1 bioactivity due to the materials' biocompatibility. Quantitative analysis is achieved by the signal-off HQ peak current, which is inversely proportional to CYFRA 21-1 concentration, with two linear ranges of 0.010-5.0 and 5.0-25 ng mL-1 on a logarithmic concentration scale and a detection limit of 3.0 pg mL-1. Moreover, the sensor exhibits high specificity, reliable reproducibility, and exceptional stability. Simultaneously, the proposed competitive immunosensor can effectively detect CYFRA 21-1 in human serum samples, demonstrating good recovery. The implementation of this electrochemical biosensor offers an opportunity to develop an accurate, cost-effective, and user-friendly diagnostic tool for detecting this type of cancer.

papers.abstract_en: We investigated whether carbon nanoparticles (CNPs), a shared core component of coal dust, ambient PM2.5, and tobacco smoke, drive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progression. In an ectopic xenograft model (nude mice pre‑exposed to 15 µg/kg CNPs for 1 week, subsequently inoculated with A549/A427 cells with or without ARNT2 silencing, with CNP administration continued for a total of 40 days), CNP exposure increased tumor volume at day 36 (A549, 194 ± 17-308 ± 22 mm³; A427, 245 ± 31-417 ± 42 mm³), proliferation (Ki‑67/PCNA: A549, 2.93‑/3.33-fold; A427, 1.94‑/3.55-fold), and levels of epithelial-mesenchymal transition markers (N‑cadherin/Vimentin: A549, 1.61‑/3.17-fold; A427, 2.44‑/1.98-fold), while ARNT2 knockdown reversed these effects. In vitro, CNP treatment (2 µg/mL, 48 h) enhanced proliferation (A549, 2.01‑fold; A427, 1.43-fold), migration (A549, 1.83‑fold; A427, 3.61‑fold), invasion (A549, 2.50‑fold; A427, 2.40‑fold), levels of stemness markers (CD133/SOX2/Oct4: A549, 2.38-/1.93-/2.02-fold; A427, 2.44-/1.44-/1.60-fold), and concentrations of inflammatory cytokines (TNF‑α/IL‑1β/IL‑6: A549, 5.39‑/6.41-/13.70-fold; A427, 3.59‑/10.02-/9.66-fold), reduced apoptosis (A549, 0.47‑fold; A427, 0.36-fold) and senescence (A549, 0.61-fold; A427, 0.37-fold), and increased reactive oxygen species levels (A549, 2.32‑fold; A427, 2.01‑fold); all these changes were attenuated by ARNT2 silencing. Transcriptomic and bioinformatic analyses identified ADP-ribosylation factor-like protein 14 (ARL14) as a downstream effector of ARNT2; ARL14 overexpression in ARNT2‑silenced cells restored proliferation and invasion and reduced apoptosis. Overall, experimental CNP exposure promotes NSCLC progression in an ARNT2-dependent manner, with ARL14 as a downstream mediator, which suggests potential targets for intervention in particulate-associated lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: B7-H3 is widely expressed in multiple solid tumors but shows minimal expression in normal tissues, making it an ideal target for molecular imaging; however, its systematic investigation remains limited. In this study, we utilized the clinically investigated B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) HS-20093 to develop and evaluate a novel immuno-positron emission tomography (immuno-PET) tracer, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093, for accurate imaging of B7-H3 expression in lung cancer and triple-negative breast cancer models. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 enables sensitive immuno-PET imaging of B7-H3 and reveals tumor-type-dependent differences in B7-H3 expression and intracellular behavior.

The chemical components of PT-EAE were identified using Ultra-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Quadrupole-Orbitrap Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Exactive-Orbitrap-MS). Network pharmacology was employed to predict the potential active components of PT-EAE and their molecular targets affecting NSCLC cell functions. A "PT-EAE-active components-targets-disease" interaction network was constructed. Gene Ontology (GO) functional annotation and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis were performed on the potential targets to identify core targets and signaling pathways closely related to the active components of PT-EAE. Subsequently, in A549 cells, the effects of PT-EAE alone, DDP alone, and their combination (PT-EAE & DDP) were evaluated. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, wound healing assay, transwell assay, and flow cytometry were used to detect cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis, respectively. Finally, western blotting and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were utilized to detect the expression levels and phosphorylation status of the predicted core molecular proteins following treatment with PT-EAE and DDP. PT-EAE inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of A549 cells, while promoting apoptosis. Compared to the DDP monotherapy group, the PT-EAE & DDP combination group reduced the IC50 of DDP for inhibiting A549 cell proliferation. Network pharmacology analysis identified 12 active components in PT-EAE, which were mapped to 124 NSCLC-related targets and multiple key signaling pathways. Among these, EGFR, Src, and PI3K were identified as potential core nodes. At the molecular level, PT-EAE downregulated the protein expression levels of EGFR and Src in A549 cells, as well as the phosphorylation levels of downstream molecules in the Src signaling pathway-PI3K, Akt, and mTOR. It also suppressed the mRNA expression of EGFR, Src, PI3K, Akt, and mTOR. The ethyl acetate extract of Tumor Vine, when combined with cisplatin, shows promising anti-tumor activity through multi-component, multi-target, and multi-pathway actions, with the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway likely representing one of its therapeutic routes.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. RESULTS: Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. CONCLUSIONS: Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.

papers.abstract_en: A 72-year-old woman with a history of resected lung adenocarcinoma presented with a pancreatic mass and multiple bilateral renal masses. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition of the pancreatic lesion showed neuroendocrine morphology, synaptophysin positivity, focal chromogranin A positivity, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 2%, leading to an initial diagnosis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grade 1. Renal biopsy also demonstrated neuroendocrine differentiation with a Ki-67 labeling index of 17%. However, the pancreatic lesion was hypovascular and poorly defined, and the multifocal bilateral renal involvement was atypical for a low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. Re-evaluation of the resected lung specimen revealed a focal neuroendocrine component showing large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma-like features, although the strict diagnostic criteria for such a diagnosis were not fully met. Genomic analysis identified a KRAS G12V mutation shared by the renal and lung tumors, supporting the interpretation that the renal lesions represented metastatic recurrence of the previously resected lung tumor. Direct molecular confirmation was unavailable for the pancreatic lesion because of insufficient residual endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition material; therefore, its origin remained diagnostically uncertain. Nevertheless, based on the overall clinicopathological context, the pancreatic lesion was interpreted as an accompanying neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion most consistent with metastatic recurrence. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical history, imaging features, disease distribution, archival pathology, and molecular findings when evaluating neuroendocrine tumor-like lesions in patients with a prior malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the genetic, epigenetic, and molecular drivers of this heterogeneous disease, metabolic reprogramming has only recently emerged as a major determinant of tumour progression and therapeutic response. Cumulative evidence demonstrates that rather than relying on a single nutrient source or pathway, cancer cells integrate glucose and glutamine, fatty acid and one-carbon metabolism, as well as nucleotide biosynthesis, and redox-supporting circuits in a highly context-dependent manner. These programs vary across histological and molecular subtypes, reflecting the influence of lineage identity and oncogenic state on metabolic organisation. In both non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer, subtype-specific constraints shape distinct metabolic states, yet a common feature is the ability to rapidly shift between alternative nutrients and biosynthetic routes. This adaptability supports continued growth under nutrient limitation, maintains redox homeostasis, and contributes to resistance against conventional and targeted therapies. By summarising current mechanistic evidence, this review presents lung cancer metabolism as an integrated and adaptable system rather than a collection of isolated pathways, and identifies metabolic dependencies that may be leveraged for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: Although climate change represents one of the greatest public health challenges of our time, its impacts on patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unclear. This Personal View synthesises the evidence surrounding established, emerging, and postulated climate change health effects on patients with ILD, who are especially vulnerable to disease due to older age, reduced lung function, and sensitivity to inhaled exposures. Established risk factors for ILD such as air pollution might worsen with climate change, whereas other exposures such as extreme heat, viral illnesses, residential water intrusion, pollen, natural disasters, and desertification could pose novel threats to this population. Knowledge gaps exist across multiple domains, including wildfire smoke effects, the effects of climate on occupational ILD, and disaster preparedness. The incorporation of multiple research modalities, including patient-centred approaches, is crucial to address these gaps. Clinicians, scientists, and professional societies can lead climate-health research, the adoption of mitigation and adaptation strategies, and drive global policy actions to address this growing challenge.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Achalasia is associated with an increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma even after definitive surgical treatment. Heller-Dor surgery is an established surgical treatment for achalasia; however, marked esophageal dilatation may persist despite successful symptom control and pose technical challenges during subsequent esophagectomy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old man with a history of Heller-Dor surgery for achalasia and prior endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma developed a metachronous lesion at a different esophageal site. Histopathological examination after ESD demonstrated deep submucosal and vascular invasion, warranting additional curative treatment. Preoperative imaging showed predominant upper thoracic esophageal dilatation with a maximum diameter of 56 mm, whereas gastric deformity was minimal. The patient underwent prone-position video-assisted thoracoscopic subtotal esophagectomy with 3-field lymphadenectomy and retrosternal gastric conduit reconstruction. Intraoperatively, venous engorgement required meticulous dissection, while marked upper thoracic esophageal dilatation restricted the operative workspace around the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. An internal organ retractor provided stable esophageal traction with flexible repositioning of the traction point, facilitating adequate exposure. Despite intra-abdominal adhesions from the previous surgery, gastric conduit reconstruction was successfully completed as anticipated from the preoperative assessment of gastric anatomy. Final histopathological examination revealed no residual carcinoma or lymph node metastasis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained recurrence-free at 2 years. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term endoscopic surveillance remains important after surgical treatment for achalasia. In patients requiring subsequent esophagectomy, preoperative assessment of the degree and distribution of esophageal dilatation may help anticipate technical difficulty, while appropriate repositionable traction may facilitate operative exposure. Careful assessment of gastric anatomy may also help determine the feasibility of gastric conduit reconstruction after Heller-Dor surgery.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is among the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Previous treatment regimens often have limited efficacy due to drug resistance and recurrence. Metabolic reprogramming participates in the initiation and progression of NSCLC, with prominent changes in lipid metabolism. Mutations in specific driver genes directly remodel lipid metabolic reprogramming in NSCLC by rewiring lipid synthesis, uptake, and catabolism, which confers cancer cells with enhanced proliferative and metastatic capacity. On this basis, targeted lipid metabolism reprogramming has become a promising new direction for the treatment of NSCLC. In this review, we examined the alterations in lipid metabolism in NSCLC, explored the mechanisms by which driver gene mutations change lipid metabolism in NSCLC, and provided possible therapeutic strategies targeting key lipid metabolism pathways at the current stage, aiming to offer a theoretical basis and prospects for the development of novel therapies targeting specific gene mutation subtypes of NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: GFPT1, the rate-limiting enzyme of the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway, promotes various cancers but its role in esophageal cancer is unclear. GFPT1 expression was assessed by public datasets, western blotting, and IHC. GFPT1-silenced cells were established via siRNA. Proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, ER stress, and autophagy markers were evaluated by CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell, wound healing, flow cytometry, western blotting, and LC3 immunofluorescence. In addition, rescue experiments were performed using the ER stress inhibitor 4-PBA in GFPT1-knockdown cells, and O-GlcNAcylation levels were examined by western blot. GFPT1 was highly expressed in esophageal cancer tissues. Knockdown of GFPT1 suppressed proliferation, invasion, and migration, while enhancing apoptosis. GFPT1 depletion upregulated ER stress markers (GRP78, GRP94, p-PERK, p-eIF2α) and autophagy-related changes (increased LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, ATG5, ATG7, and reduced p62), and reduced overall O-GlcNAcylation. Importantly, treatment with 4-PBA significantly reversed the GFPT1 knockdown-induced suppression of proliferation, migration, and invasion, and rescued the alterations in ER stress markers, indicating that the phenotypic effects are causally mediated, at least in part, through the ER stress pathway. GFPT1 knockdown impedes esophageal cancer progression by reducing aggressive phenotypes and promoting apoptosis, potentially via ER stress and autophagy activation.

papers.abstract_en: Sanguinarine (SAN), a natural alkaloid derived from Papaveraceae plants, is an active component in traditional Chinese medicines. SAN exerts inhibitory effects on tumor cells, but research on its effects on lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and the underlying mechanisms remains limited. The Hippo signaling pathway is commonly downregulated in LUAD, making it a key target for therapeutic intervention. Our study reveals that SAN significantly inhibits LUAD. Mechanistically, SAN bound to Large Tumor Suppressor 1 (LATS1) and promoted its phosphorylation, thereby activating the Hippo pathway and pyroptosis in LUAD. Notably, YAP overexpression inhibited pyroptosis and weakened the antitumor effect of SAN, further confirming that SAN exerts its antitumor effects by regulating the Hippo-YAP axis. Findings from both in vivo experiments and single-cell RNA sequencing consistently show that SAN remodels the tumor immune microenvironment and inhibits tumor growth. Specifically, we observed significant changes in the tumor microenvironment, including increased CD8+ T cell infiltration and a notably reduced number of myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblasts. Collectively, our findings establish SAN as a candidate therapeutic agent that exerts antitumor effects through dual modulation of the Hippo-mediated pyroptosis pathway and tumor immunity, providing a mechanistic basis for its potential clinical application in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) is characterized by alveolar fibrin deposition, driven by dysregulated hypercoagulation and impaired fibrinolysis. Although alveolar epithelial type II (AEC II) cells contribute to this imbalance by overexpressing Tissue Factor (TF) and Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), the upstream regulatory mechanisms, particularly at the epitranscriptomic level, remain unclear. The potential role of the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA demethylase FTO in ARDS pathogenesis is unexplored. METHODS: In this study, we employed lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced rat ARDS models and LPS-stimulated AEC II cells as primary experimental systems to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Multi-omics profiling, combining methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), was performed. Gain and loss-of-function studies were conducted using lentiviral vectors both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations involved MeRIP-qPCR, mRNA stability assays, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), Western blot, immunofluorescence, and pharmacological modulation of the NF-κB pathway. RESULTS: Lungs from ARDS rats showed decreased global levels and increased FTO expression. Knockdown of FTO alleviated lung injury, reduced pulmonary edema, and suppressed the expression of TF and PAI-1, concomitant with inhibition of NF-κB signaling. Integrated multi-omics analysis identified Protein Kinase C Beta (PRKCB), a serine/threonine kinase known to regulate inflammatory signaling, as a key target of FTO. Mechanistically, FTO-mediated demethylation of PRKCB mRNA reduced its recognition by reader proteins that typically promote mRNA decay, thereby prolonging its half-life and enhancing protein translation. Elevated PRKCB promoted IKKβ phosphorylation and subsequent NF-κB activation. Rescue experiments confirmed that FTO regulates alveolar hypercoagulation and fibrinolytic inhibition in ARDS via PRKCB-dependent activation of the NF-κB pathway. CONCLUSION: Our study identifies the FTO-PRKCB-NF-κB axis as a novel epitranscriptomic pathway driving alveolar fibrin deposition in ARDS. These findings reveal FTO as a potential therapeutic target for mitigating alveolar hypercoagulation and fibrinolysis inhibition in ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (BPDE), a key carcinogenic metabolite of the ubiquitous environmental pollutant benzo[a]pyrene, is a well-established etiological agent in lung cancer. However, a systems-level understanding of its molecular targets and pathogenic mechanisms remains incomplete. This study aimed to identify and characterize the core toxicity targets linking BPDE exposure to lung carcinogenesis using an integrative network toxicology approach. METHODS: Putative BPDE targets were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction and TargetNet. Lung cancer-associated genes were compiled from GeneCards and TCGA datasets. The intersection yielded candidate genes, which were analyzed via protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, functional enrichment, and machine learning (LASSO, XGBoost, Random Forest, Boruta) to identify core biomarkers. A nomogram was developed for risk prediction. The key target CA2 was further validated for prognostic value, differential expression across multiple cohorts (TCGA, GEO), and associated biological pathways via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and pathway activity scoring. Molecular docking was performed to simulate the BPDE-CA2 interaction. RESULTS: Thirty-one overlapping targets were identified. Enrichment analysis implicated processes like inflammation, oxidative stress response, and cancer-related pathways (e.g. p53, cell cycle). Machine learning convergence highlighted four core biomarkers: PARP1, ALOX5, CA9, and CA2. Among these, CA2 demonstrated significant prognostic value, consistent downregulation in lung tumor tissues across independent datasets, and distinct molecular phenotypes: its high expression correlated with immune activation and suppressed VEGF signaling, while low expression was linked to enhanced cell cycle activity. Molecular docking revealed a stable binding interaction between BPDE and CA2. CONCLUSION: This integrative study identifies a set of core targets, prominently featuring CA2, that potentially mediate BPDE-induced lung carcinogenesis. CA2 downregulation is associated with poor prognosis, a pro-proliferative phenotype, and may be directly modulated by BPDE, positioning it as a critical molecular link between environmental exposure and lung cancer development. Insight Paragraph This study provides a systems-level molecular bridge connecting environmental carcinogen exposure to lung cancer pathogenesis. By integrating network toxicology, machine learning, and multi-omics validation, we move beyond single-gene associations to identify a core set of toxicity targets, most notably CA2. We demonstrate that CA2 downregulation, potentially via direct interaction with BPDE, is linked to poor prognosis and a pro-proliferative phenotype. This integrative approach offers a novel mechanistic insight, positioning CA2 as a critical node at the intersection of environmental exposure, disrupted metabolism, and tumor progression, with implications for risk prediction and targeted prevention strategies.

papers.abstract_en: We herein describe the structure-based design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a new class of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) inhibitors guided by X-ray crystal structures of our previously identified compounds 13-15. X-ray co-crystal structures of second-generation inhibitors 19b (Subseries I) and 20b (Subseries II) within zHDAC6 CD2 confirmed that these compounds behave as highly potent HDAC6 inhibitors with the ability to engage the S531 residue in the L2 loop HDAC6 catalytic domain. Western-blot analysis confirmed the target engagement in cell-based settings, through the increase of acetylated tubulin levels, without significant variation in the histone acetylation status. Compound 20b extensively reduced the viability of A549 cells in both 2- and 3-dimensional cell cultures, through the activation of pro-autophagic pathways. In addition, HDAC6 inhibition impaired the nucleation of stress-granules, confirming the ability of these compounds to modulate liquid-liquid phase separation, an emerging HDAC6-driven hallmark in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x-ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP-based diagnostics, from benchtop to high-fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

papers.abstract_en: The assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples maps accessible chromatin in archival tissues, but DNA degradation and crosslinking remain significant challenges when processing these samples. Here, we present a protocol for Omni-ATAC-seq on degraded human small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) FFPE-derived samples. We detail steps for successful nuclei isolation, efficient tagmentation, and optimal library amplification to overcome the low signal-to-noise ratio. This protocol enables high-quality epigenetic profiling, turning archived SCLC samples into valuable resources for studying disease progression. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Kawasaki et al.1.
